name: Three Represents
summary: The Three Represents is Jiang Zemin's doctrine that the Chinese Communist Party must always represent the development of China's advanced productive forces, its advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the overwhelming majority of the people. It makes economic development the first test of the Party's progressiveness, welcomes private entrepreneurs and professionals as builders of socialism and as Party members, keeps Party leadership, public ownership in the lead and the Four Cardinal Principles, and rejects Western multi-party and separation-of-powers models. It was written into the Party constitution in 2002.
scope: The doctrine in Jiang Zemin's own texts: his 2000-2001 Three Represents speeches (including the 1 July 2001 speech), his report to the 16th Party Congress (2002) and the Party constitution as amended in 2002. Positions that Jiang states there as part of the Party's guiding line count, including the Four Cardinal Principles and the socialist market economy as he restates them; Marxism-Leninism, Mao Zedong Thought and Deng Xiaoping Theory as separate bodies, general CCP policy outside these texts, and later Xi Jinping Thought are left out.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The 2002 report gives the market a basic role in allocating resources but only under the state's macroeconomic control and beside a dominant public sector, so it neither endorses free markets over government nor the reverse.

public-ownership.rationale: The 16th Congress report says to consolidate the public sector unswervingly, that state control of the economy's lifeline is of crucial importance, and that the central government is investor in large enterprises, infrastructure and important natural resources, with the state holding controlling shares in lifeline firms.

cut-welfare.rationale: The report asks to improve pensions, medical insurance, unemployment insurance and subsistence allowances and to develop social relief and welfare programmes, which a call to cut welfare would contradict; the Party does not call for much more than a level suited to development.

central-planning.rationale: Jiang calls the shift from the planned economy to the socialist market economy a historic breakthrough that opened new prospects, and the report assigns the market the basic role in allocating resources.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The report makes the state the investor in large enterprises, infrastructure and important natural resources vital to the economy and security, gives priority to the information industry, and says policy guidance should help form large competitive firms.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The doctrine holds that public ownership plays the dominant role and that the state sector must control the economy's lifeline, so it does not put property in many small hands rather than the state, though it also promotes small private firms and more family property.

one-party-rule.rationale: Jiang's 2001 speech says that without strong CPC leadership the country would fall into a mess and break up, the Four Cardinal Principles include leadership by the Party, and the Party constitution makes it the core of leadership of the state under Marxism-Leninism.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Jiang keeps the basic Marxist tenets about capitalism as true for Western capitalism, but says private entrepreneurs in China are builders of socialism whose legitimate income is protected and calls for a fresh study of labour value in a socialist society.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The report makes distribution according to work dominant while letting labour, capital, technology and management share in income by contribution and protecting all legitimate income 'from work or not'.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Jiang says the Marxist labour-value theory described capitalist conditions and must be restudied for a socialist society, and the report names work, knowledge, technology, management and capital as all sources of social wealth, so the doctrine does not hold that labour alone creates value.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The report says to give priority to efficiency with due consideration to fairness and to guard against excessive income disparity 'while opposing equalitarianism', so equal outcomes are rejected as an aim.

rich-first.rationale: The report encourages part of the people to become rich first through honest labour and lawful operations, and Jiang's July 2001 speech says that when some people and regions get rich first, others will be brought along toward common prosperity.

moral-incentives.rationale: The report lets labour, capital, technology and management share in income by contribution and the 2001 speech asks for pay for talented people to be commensurate with their contributions, so material reward stays the main spur even though the Party also urges devotion.

collective-farming.rationale: The report says to keep stabilising and improving the household contract management system in the countryside and to respect farm households as market players, which excludes collective farming.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Party constitution calls reform and opening up the only way to make the country strong and demands all-dimensional opening, and the report urges more trade, foreign investment and going out, the opposite of a closed bloc.

delink-world-market.rationale: The report promotes economic globalisation in a direction conducive to common prosperity so that all countries, developing ones in particular, can benefit, rather than breaking ties with rich countries.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The report credits a proactive fiscal policy with overcoming the Asian crisis and Jiang's economic work speech calls for issuing treasury bonds to expand domestic demand, though neither names deficit size.

farm-price-support.rationale: Jiang's November 2000 economic work speech says to continue buying surplus grain from farmers without limit at protective prices to protect farmers' interests.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The report requires that controlling shares in lifeline enterprises be held by the state and asks for national economic security to be safeguarded in opening up, which leaves no room for foreign control of such firms, but it grants foreign investors national treatment elsewhere.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The report keeps basic pension and medical systems that combine socially pooled funds with personal contributions, so it does not move pensions wholly to private individual accounts.

job-guarantee.rationale: Jiang says the planned system once took care of urban employment and that people must change their mentality, find jobs themselves and accept flexible work, while the report gives governments a duty to create jobs rather than a guarantee.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The 2002 report calls developing a market economy under socialism a historic contribution of the Communists, and says the market economy, democracy and culture are to be developed 'under the firm leadership of the CPC'.

social-market-economy.rationale: The report pairs a socialist market economy with a social security system and fair competition rules, rejecting the planned economy, but keeps public ownership dominant rather than a social market on private ownership.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The report says the state should give the western region greater support through investment, tax policy and transfer payments, and Jiang tells coastal regions to help the central and western areas.

abolish-ip.rationale: The report asks to improve the system of intellectual property rights protection and to win independent intellectual property rights in key technologies.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The report relies on the state to improve social insurance, subsistence allowances and social relief and welfare programmes, not on charities and local communities in place of government.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The doctrine gives the state macroeconomic control, a dominant public sector, a social security system and a lead role in culture, which a state limited to defence, justice and property would contradict.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Jiang's economic work speech calls for stepping up oil exploration in the west and offshore to raise oil and gas reserves and for making full use of China's rich coal resources.

state-harmful.rationale: The doctrine's cornerstone is a Party that exercises state power through the people's democratic dictatorship, so a view that the state is unnecessary could not be held with it.

taxation-theft.rationale: The report and Jiang's economic work speech treat taxation as a legitimate state function, calling for stronger collection and administration of taxes and for tax-for-fees reform in rural areas.

decide-locally.rationale: Jiang's 2001 speech says guiding principles, policies and the legal system must be consistent and centralised and no locality should go its own way, although the report also gives local governments investor functions and grassroots self-government.

revolution-justified.rationale: Jiang's 80th anniversary speech presents the revolution that overthrew the Kuomintang and founded the PRC as the Party's historic task and the October Revolution as the event that brought Marxism-Leninism to China.

political-violence-never.rationale: The 2001 speech honours the armed seizure of power in the revolutionary wars, and Jiang's report and speech both say the state will never undertake to renounce the use of force against Taiwan independence.

democracy-best.rationale: The report praises socialist democracy as having strong vitality and superiority, but insists on Party leadership, says never to copy Western political models and resists multi-party competition, so it does not accept voters' choices as final.

direct-votes.rationale: The doctrine rests political power on the people's congress system, with direct popular exercise of rights confined to grassroots self-government, not citizens voting on major laws.

workers-councils.rationale: The Four Cardinal Principles and the report make the people's congresses, led by the Party, the system of political power, with workers' conferences only inside enterprises.

right-to-secede.rationale: The report says China's sovereignty and territorial integrity brook no division and opposes all separatist activity, and the Party constitution ties national unity to the Party's mission.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The report places courts and procuratorates in the state's judicial system and puts the army under the Party's absolute leadership, which privately run courts, policing or defence would contradict.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Jiang says that, since Communists are atheists, the spiritual core of society cannot be any religion, and the report says the Constitution and laws embody the Party's views and the people's will.

clerical-rule.rationale: Jiang rules out any religion as the spiritual core of society and puts supreme political authority in the Party, so clergy could not hold the highest authority.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Jiang's 2001 speech says the power in Party hands is given by the people and that the Party exercises state power for the people, not from any divine source.

separated-powers.rationale: In his 2001 speech Jiang says to resist resolutely the impact of Western political models such as the multi-party system or separation of powers among executive, legislative and judicial branches.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Party constitution and Jiang's 2001 speech define the CPC as the vanguard of the working class that must stay its leading core, armed with Marxist theory and requiring members to join ideologically as well as organisationally.

party-controls-media.rationale: Jiang tells the publicity directors to keep public opinion work firmly under Party leadership and to tighten management of the Internet, and the report calls for correct guidance of opinion by the press, radio and television.

party-commands-army.rationale: The report calls the Party's absolute leadership over the army the eternal soul of the army and the Party constitution commits the Party to lead the PLA.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Article 10 of the Party constitution makes the minority subordinate to the majority and lower organisations to higher ones, and the report says decisions must be carried out without fail and nobody may go their own way.

leader-cult.rationale: Article 10 of the 2002 Party constitution says the Party forbids all forms of personality cult, and Jiang says nobody may have the final say alone in a Party committee.

people-in-arms.rationale: The report builds a modernised professional army on the road of fewer but better troops and keeps the militia only as support, which replacing the army with an armed citizenry would contradict.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The report says nobody has a privilege to overstep the Constitution and laws and that Party members and cadres must set an example in obeying them, so a ruler above law is not the stated doctrine.

office-by-exam.rationale: Jiang's 2001 speech asks for open, fair competition on merit for appointment and promotion and the report for a merit-based public servant system, though the Party also appoints cadres by political integrity and keeps hold of cadre affairs.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The report asks that there be laws to go by, that laws be observed and strictly enforced and that arbitrary decision-making be prevented, and names ruling by law the basic principle of the Party in leading the country.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The report asks for a system of keeping the public informed and for government affairs to be made known, and Jiang says Party members and ordinary people should have more right to know in cadre selection.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The report promises that people directly exercise democratic rights in villager and urban resident self-government and in workers' conferences, but within Party leadership and in an orderly way.

independent-unions.rationale: The report and the Party constitution both say to strengthen the Party's leadership over trade unions and mass organisations, and Party organisations in firms lead the unions.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Jiang calls the work of 'democratic movement elements' with hostile forces a main form of the class struggle that continues, the report says to guard against subversive and separatist activity and crack down on cult gangs, and Party committees are to lead non-governmental organisations.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The report says the country should never copy any model of the Western political system, and the 2001 speech says each country's history, culture, social system and development model should be respected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The report calls for improving procuratorial, judicial and public security work and cracking down on criminal activity according to law, with comprehensive measures to keep public order.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Party constitution and Jiang's speech make permanent, disciplined Party organisation under democratic centralism the means of struggle, with factions and small cliques opposed.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The Party is the doctrine's channel between people and leadership, working through the mass line and Party-led mass organisations, so bypassing parties is not its position.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The report says crime is to be dealt with according to law and that all people are equal before the law, so killing suspects without trial contradicts it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The report says all people must be equal before the law and that none may have a privilege to overstep the Constitution and laws, though the doctrine says nothing on moral worth itself and its record on legal equality is mixed.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Jiang says decadent culture that corrodes people's minds should be resisted through policies, systems, education and management and the report calls for managing the market for cultural products.

more-religion-public.rationale: Jiang says Communists are atheists and that the spiritual core of society cannot be any religion, and the report has religions adapt to socialist society and be handled according to law, though it keeps freedom of religious belief.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The report calls carrying forward and cultivating the five-thousand-year national spirit a crucial task of cultural development and supports protecting major cultural heritage, while Jiang says to discard the dross and keep the essence.

gradual-change.rationale: The report asks that reform be promoted progressively, with stability of overriding importance and the pace set by what society can bear, though it also urges breaking out of outdated systems.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The report and Jiang's 2001 speech say states should not resort to the use or threat of force, should not interfere in one another's internal affairs, and treat US-led NATO action over Yugoslavia as an attack.

limit-growth.rationale: Jiang calls development the absolute need and the Party constitution makes economic development the central task, so growth is not to be limited, with the environment weighed within sustainable development.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The doctrine presents China as a multi-ethnic nation of 56 groups united under equality, solidarity and mutual assistance, not one to be made up mainly of a single ethnic group.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Jiang names the productive forces the ultimate decisive force of social development and says class struggle persists in a limited scope but is no longer the principal contradiction, which Holbig reads as a shift of attention from class relations.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Jiang tells Party members to resist money worship, hedonism and out-and-out egoism and the doctrine names collectivism the principle of morality, though it allows lawful individual interests.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Jiang's speeches ask for a balance between respect for lawful individual rights and shouldering social obligations, with collectivism as the guiding principle, so they do not rank duties plainly first.

limit-population.rationale: The report names family planning a basic state policy and says to keep the birthrate low.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The report calls accomplishing industrialisation an arduous historical task and an inevitable trend of modernisation and sets a new road of industrialisation, which could not be squared with calling industrial civilisation a disaster.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Jiang calls science and technology the primary productive force, asks for leapfrog development and says practices and regulations that impede development must be changed, while keeping stability of overriding importance.

restore-past-order.rationale: The doctrine demands keeping pace with the times and freeing minds from outdated notions and systems, putting progress ahead of restoring a past order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Jiang calls practice the sole criterion of truth and judges work by its benefit to productive forces, but also says the Four Cardinal Principles and Marxism must never be abandoned.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A return to a hunter-gatherer life could not be held alongside the doctrine's central goal of socialist modernisation, industrialisation and rising living standards.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Four Cardinal Principles uphold the people's democratic dictatorship led by the working class and based on the worker-peasant alliance, which is broader than the statement's working class over the former ruling classes until classes disappear.

organic-representation.rationale: The doctrine represents citizens through people's congresses and Party leadership, with trade unions and other bodies led by the Party, so it does not put families, communities and trade bodies in the place of parties.

total-state.rationale: The report separates government functions from enterprise management, gives the market the basic role in allocation and cuts administrative approvals, although the Party leads culture and education.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Party's stated mission is the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation after a century of humiliation, though it pursues it by reform and modernisation rather than a radical break and names no decadence of its own.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The report says China will never seek hegemony and never go in for expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The doctrine locates authority in the Party's constitution, laws and collective decisions and condemns feudal relations and thinking, not personal oaths between lords and followers.

bound-labor.rationale: Jiang's 2001 speech says the revolution aimed to eliminate exploitation by the landlord class and to change feudal relations of production.

single-common-good.rationale: The report says the fundamental interests of the whole people are identical, yet also tells the Party to balance the interests of different quarters and groups.

rule-by-example.rationale: The report makes ruling by law the Party's basic principle and treats the rule of virtue as complementary to it, with cadres' exemplary conduct a duty, so it does not rely on moral example more than law.

national-self-determination.rationale: The 2001 speech backs Asian, African and Latin American peoples fighting for national independence, yet the report denies the right of Taiwan and the country's minorities to separate.

force-without-un.rationale: Jiang says states should abide by the UN Charter's purposes and principles, settle disputes by dialogue and not resort to the use or threat of force.

class-collaboration.rationale: Jiang says Party policy should unite people of all strata, treats private entrepreneurs as builders of socialism, calls the fundamental interests of the people identical and puts class struggle outside the principal contradiction.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The report supports the protection of major cultural heritage and Jiang says to carry forward the fine cultural traditions, which contradicts sacrificing inherited cultural institutions.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The doctrine's ethnic policy is equality, solidarity and mutual assistance among all ethnic groups and it condemns imperialist privilege, which a law segregating races would contradict.

population-transfer.rationale: Pressing a minority seen as hostile to leave could not be squared with the report's policy of equality, solidarity and mutual assistance among all ethnic groups.

national-mission.rationale: The report says countries with different social systems and roads should respect one another and that no country should impose its will on others.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Jiang cites Lenin's conclusion that socialist revolution could succeed first in one or several countries and builds socialism in China without waiting for revolutions elsewhere.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Jiang calls the Soviet Union 'a socialist country that had developed for more than 70 years' and treats its disintegration as a setback of world socialism.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The report concedes that corruption is conspicuous in some places and that formalism and bureaucracy among some leading cadres can divorce the Party from the masses, while holding the Party's course correct.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Jiang praises the Party's part in the world struggle against fascism and holds communism to be the Party's highest ideal, so equating the two as totalitarianisms is rejected.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The Party constitution says class struggle will persist for a long time within a limited scope though no longer the principal contradiction, while Jiang calls the Cultural Revolution's class-struggle line a grave deviation.

land-redistribution.rationale: Jiang praises the Party for leading the people to expropriate local tyrants and allocate land, and says the new-democratic revolution eliminated the landlord class, though he describes it as past policy.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The doctrine's territorial claims rest on sovereignty and the pledge of non-expansion rather than on the presence of co-nationals abroad.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Jiang says advanced capitalist countries have adapted through taxation, welfare and state intervention and eased class contradictions, while holding that the basic contradictions of capitalism remain.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Jiang's 2001 speech describes imperialist rule that made China semi-colonial as repression, praises peoples fighting for independence and opposes hegemonism.

patriotic-education.rationale: The report calls for promoting patriotism, building national self-esteem and pride, and putting the national spirit into national education, especially for youth.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The doctrine condemns the imperialist privileges and semi-colonial status imposed on China and counts anti-colonial independence struggles on the side of justice.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Party constitution says the realisation of communism is the highest ideal and ultimate goal of the Party.

defeat-communism.rationale: Communism is the Party's ultimate goal and Jiang calls talk that Marxism will die out idle chatter.

religious-nation.rationale: Jiang defines the Chinese nation as a union of 56 ethnic groups with a five-thousand-year national spirit and says the spiritual core cannot be any religion.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Jiang treats feudal autocracy and monarchy as what the 1911 revolution and the Party's revolution ended, and the Party is atheist, so a sacred hereditary ruler has no place in the doctrine.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The doctrine holds that the Party's Marxist leadership is legitimate and that no religion may be the spiritual core, so removing rulers for not governing by religious law contradicts it.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Jiang states the materialist thesis that social being determines thinking and treats ideological struggle as a form of class struggle, not a spiritual contest of good and evil.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Jiang says the Party cherishes the memory of revolutionary martyrs and the report asks for preferential treatment for martyrs' families, although the Party is atheist and would not call them saints.

simple-living.rationale: The doctrine's principal contradiction is the people's ever-growing material and cultural needs, and the report aims to raise consumption, which limiting needs would contradict.

property-franchise.rationale: Jiang calls it improper to judge anyone's political standing by whether or how much property they own and asks that all people exercise democratic election rights.

racial-franchise.rationale: The report's ethnic policy of equality and unity and its call for the people of all ethnic groups to be masters of the country rule out confining voting and office to one ethnic group.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The report and Jiang's cadre speeches ask that leaders be appointed on merit and supervised by the Party and the people, which hereditary succession of a state leader would contradict.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The report says all people are equal before the law and that none may have a privilege to overstep the Constitution and laws, and the revolution is said to have ended feudal privilege.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The report asks that religions adapt to socialist society, handle religious affairs according to law and run themselves independently.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The report speaks of a great national spirit evolved over more than 5,000 years and Jiang calls China an ancient civilisation of more than five thousand years, while stressing the break of 1949.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The report calls for modernisation together with carrying forward the fine tradition of national culture and traditional virtues, but asks only for the essence of tradition and not a return.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Jiang tells Party members to combat money worship and hedonism, while the report aims to expand consumption and raise its share of GDP.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The report adopts an active defence strategy and promises never to expand, yet Jiang says the Party will not renounce the use of force over Taiwan.

multipolar-world.rationale: The report says China will work to boost world multipolarisation, opposes hegemonism and power politics, and Jiang notes the US superpower position as a problem.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Jiang says the questions of peace and development are the question of North and South and that developed countries should support and assist developing ones under equality, fairness and mutual benefit.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The report and Jiang's 2001 speech call for a new, fair and rational international economic order and for gradually transforming the old inequitable one so that developing countries benefit.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Jiang says that under the old international economic order developed countries use their economic, technological and military superiority to obtain huge profits in the world market, and the North-South gap is widening.

non-intervention.rationale: The report and Party constitution make non-interference in other countries' internal affairs a basic principle, and Jiang says each country's affairs are for its own people to decide.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The Party constitution and report base all relations with states and parties on non-interference in internal affairs and the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The report says all countries should respect and consult one another, none should impose its will, and international relations should be democratic and equal.

party-own-road.rationale: The Party constitution and report base relations with other parties on independence and non-interference, and Jiang says the Party must take its own road suited to China's conditions.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The Party constitution names a self-reliant effort in its basic line, while the report seeks more foreign direct investment, foreign capital and technology.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The report calls strengthening national defence a strategic task and calls for modernising the army and keeping it under the Party's absolute leadership.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The report requires the army to be forever loyal to the Party, strictly disciplined and under its absolute leadership, so soldiers refusing orders in an interstate war is not its position.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Jiang says hostile Western forces have not abandoned their strategic attempt to Westernise and disintegrate China and the report points at foreign forces' attempts to interfere in reunification.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The report calls complete reunification a common aspiration of the Chinese nation and says the Taiwan question must not drag on indefinitely, with Hong Kong and Macao described as questions left over from history.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The report says China's sovereignty and territorial integrity brook no division and it will never allow anyone to separate Taiwan from China, though anything may be discussed within the one-China principle.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The report states the position of never undertaking to renounce the use of force against Taiwan separatists and foreign interference, and Jiang says it is the Communists' duty to end the separation.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The report says that after reunification Taiwan may keep its social system unchanged and enjoy a high degree of autonomy under one country, two systems, as Hong Kong and Macao do.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The Party constitution and the report commit the Party to uphold and improve the system of regional ethnic autonomy.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The doctrine holds up patriotism and socialism as joint banners and counts workers, peasants and intellectuals as the basic forces of national modernisation.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Jiang quotes Marx that social being determines thinking and says the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production, and between base and superstructure, drives social development.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Jiang cites Marx that an order does not perish before all its productive forces are developed and says advanced capitalist countries made great progress in productive forces, but he does not call capitalism progressive in so many words.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The doctrine says the people's democratic dictatorship is led by the working class through the Party as its vanguard, though the working class does not hold power directly.

municipal-property.rationale: The doctrine's basic economic system rests on dominant public ownership with other forms beside it and a state that holds lifeline assets, not on community ownership excluding both private owners and the state.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The doctrine's state is a centralised party-led system with a market economy, and Jiang says no locality should go its own way, which small self-governing communities holding property in common would contradict.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Jiang insists on centralised, unified leadership of Party and state with no locality going its own way, which confederations of local assemblies without governing power would contradict.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The report makes family planning a basic state policy and asks to keep the birthrate low, which incentives to have more children would contradict.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Jiang's Three Represents speeches, the 2002 report and the Party constitution record no position on this, and no stated principle settles it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Jiang's Three Represents speeches, the 2002 report and the Party constitution record no position on this, and no stated principle settles it.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Jiang's Three Represents speeches, the 2002 report and the Party constitution record no position on this, and no stated principle settles it.

unions-good.rationale: Jiang's Three Represents speeches, the 2002 report and the Party constitution record no position on this, and no stated principle settles it.

property-fundamental.rationale: Jiang's Three Represents speeches, the 2002 report and the Party constitution record no position on this, and no stated principle settles it.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Jiang's Three Represents speeches, the 2002 report and the Party constitution record no position on this, and no stated principle settles it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Jiang's Three Represents speeches, the 2002 report and the Party constitution record no position on this, and no stated principle settles it.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Jiang's Three Represents speeches, the 2002 report and the Party constitution record no position on this, and no stated principle settles it.

notes: Searched Jiang's Three Represents speeches, the 2002 report and the 2002 Party constitution for each theme (economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means, globalism). Answers about religion, ethnic policy and the army rest on Jiang's statements as codified in these texts; the actual record of the Party-state on rights and legal equality is mixed and is not scored here, so a few answers are capped at medium.
